<task>
Run a genuine, write-capable, REVIEW-ONLY adversarial review of SurvivorPulse ticket SST-1583, in the git worktree at C:\Users\wolff\Projects\SurvivorPulse\.claude\worktrees\affectionate-saha-e93fb0. Background: SST-1583 adds custom extra contests to SurvivorPulse pools -- a pool owner names an extra contest and assigns it to an existing NFL week (example: BetOnline runs a 500K-dollar Survivor pool that layers Thanksgiving Eve/Day plus Black Friday as extra contest slots onto the normal weekly schedule, making 19 total contest-weeks instead of 18). Game Plan and My Pools Season/Week views must insert the extra contest in place, and the strategy/optimizer engine must allocate picks for it. It has cleared its grooming approval gate (Pam/Deb/Felix unanimous APPROVE) after 12+ rounds of narrow adversarial review against an earlier genuine-Codex FAIL. Status is Ready. This is the mandatory genuine-Codex pass before build begins -- no story in this project reaches Done without one, and this ticket has never had one complete before (only narrow-scope substitute reviews, plus one prior genuine attempt whose job tracking was lost mid-run -- job id task-mtx8gbb7-lx2piw, no longer visible in any status listing).
Steps:
1. Get the current full spec. Use the script at C:\Users\wolff\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-wolff-Projects-SurvivorPulse--claude-worktrees-affectionate-saha-e93fb0\fa6cc5d2-cfff-45ad-8b3c-dee81cdfeb44\scratchpad\dump-ticket-spec.mjs to read the LIVE Notion ticket (page id 3d429ce5-833d-813e-92d8-f5192530807e) in full -- Description (approx 41K chars), Acceptance Criteria (approx 121K chars), Test Cases (approx 179K chars). Read the script first to see how to invoke it. Do NOT use a plain Notion fetch/API call -- that mechanism has repeatedly truncated this exact property, across the history of this ticket.
2. Write the full spec to tmp/cass/final-spec-SST-1583.md in the worktree (create tmp/cass/ if it does not exist; it is gitignored). If that file already exists from the lost prior attempt, do not trust it -- re-dump fresh from Notion and overwrite it regardless.
3. Do a genuine, adversarial review of the ENTIRE spec -- a full fresh read, not a narrow recheck of prior findings. Specifically hunt for:
   - Internal contradictions between the Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Cases.
   - Fabricated or unverified code citations in the spec -- spot-check a meaningful sample of cited files, functions, and line numbers against the actual live code in this worktree.
   - Testing-rule violations per this project testing.md standards, in particular: rule 7 (a fixture must be able to violate its own requirement -- for any must-NOT, branch, or precedence test case in the spec, confirm the described fixture actually builds the violating world, not just the passing one); rule 8 (a fix must be proven at its call site, not just at an extracted helper); vacuous always-passes assertions; mechanism-named test descriptions (should state the requirement, not the implementation mechanism); unlabeled characterization tests (a test pinning current behavior must say so).
   - Scope creep or scope gaps versus the founder original ask as described in the Description.
   - Anything a fresh implementer would find genuinely ambiguous or underspecified.
   This spec has already survived 12+ rounds of adversarial narrow-scope review that closed many real defects -- do not assume those rounds caught everything, and do not rubber-stamp it. Find what they missed.
4. Write your verdict to C:\Users\wolff\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-wolff-Projects-SurvivorPulse--claude-worktrees-affectionate-saha-e93fb0\fa6cc5d2-cfff-45ad-8b3c-dee81cdfeb44\scratchpad\codex-1583\result.txt as VERDICT PASS or VERDICT FAIL (literally that phrase, colon included) followed by numbered findings tagged BLOCKER, MAJOR, or MINOR, each with a one-line rationale and, where applicable, the file and line evidence you checked.
</task>
<grounding_rules>
- Every code citation in your findings must be verified by actually reading the cited file in this worktree; do not trust citations already present in the spec at face value.
- If you cannot verify a claim, whether it is the spec own claim or your own, label it explicitly as unverified rather than asserting it as fact.
- Do not fabricate line numbers, function names, or file paths.
</grounding_rules>

<action_safety>
- This run has write capability but this task is REVIEW ONLY: do not edit, create, or delete any file in the repository except tmp/cass/final-spec-SST-1583.md (the spec dump) and the result.txt file at the path given above.
- Do not run git commit, git push, or any destructive git command.
- You may freely run read-only exploration commands such as grep, reading files, and running the dump script.
</action_safety>

<structured_output_contract>
- The result.txt file must start with a single line stating the verdict, PASS or FAIL, clearly labeled.
- Followed by a numbered list of findings, each prefixed with severity (BLOCKER, MAJOR, or MINOR), a one-sentence description, and supporting evidence (quote or file plus line number).
- Also report back in your own final message: the verdict, a count of findings by severity, and the two file paths you wrote to (tmp/cass/final-spec-SST-1583.md and the result.txt path).
</structured_output_contract>

<default_follow_through_policy>
- If the dump script fails or the Notion page is unreachable, retry once with careful attention to the actual invocation contract of that script (read its source first), then report the blocker clearly in result.txt rather than fabricating spec content.
- Proceed through all four steps without pausing for confirmation.
</default_follow_through_policy>
